PART_B1.e: A hearth is the place where a cultural trait or innovation originates.

PART_B1.q: Judging another culture by the standards and values of one's own culture is:
PART_B1.e: Ethnocentrism is evaluating another culture through the lens of one's own cultural standards.

PART_B1.q: A boundary that was forcibly drawn over an existing cultural landscape, often ignoring it, is called:
PART_B1.e: Superimposed boundaries are drawn (often by an outside colonial power) without regard to existing cultural patterns.

o: A state gaining new territory through conquest
A central government granting more autonomy to regions within the state
A state losing all sovereignty to a supranational body
PART_B2.e: Devolution is the transfer of increased autonomy from a central government to regional governments.

PART_B2.q: Which of these is an example of a centripetal force within a state?
PART_B2.e: A shared national language unifies a state and strengthens cohesion — a centripetal force.

PART_B2.q: The practice of drawing electoral districts to concentrate opposition voters into as few districts as possible is called:
PART_B2.e: 'Packing' concentrates opposition voters into few districts, reducing their overall influence.

PART_B2.q: A state whose population shares a single, unifying cultural identity that matches its political borders is best described as a:
PART_B2.e: A nation-state is a state whose borders closely align with a single nation's cultural identity.

PART_C.q: Written response: choose TWO concepts from different units and construct an argument connecting them. Cite specific evidence from each.
o: Names both concepts precisely, gives concrete evidence for each, and explains the causal/logical bridge
Lists the two topics without connecting them
Describes only one concept in detail
Gives a personal opinion with no course evidence
PART_C.e: Strong responses anchor every claim in specific unit content and explain how the two concepts connect.

workedExamples.title: Natural increase rate
workedExamples.prompt: A country has a crude birth rate of 24 and a crude death rate of 8 (per 1,000 people). Find the natural increase rate and doubling time.
steps: NIR = (CBR − CDR)/10, as a percent = (24 − 8)/10 = 1.6%
Doubling time ≈ 70 / 1.6 ≈ 44 years

workedExamples.title: Population density
workedExamples.prompt: A region has 3,000,000 people on 1,500 km², of which 300 km² is farmland. Find the arithmetic and physiological densities.
steps: Arithmetic density = people / total land = 3,000,000 / 1,500
Physiological density = people / arable land = 3,000,000 / 300

workedExamples.title: Dependency ratio
workedExamples.prompt: A country has 25% of people under 15, 65% ages 15–64, and 10% over 64. Find the dependency ratio.
steps: Dependents = under 15 + over 64 = 25 + 10 = 35
Ratio = dependents / working-age × 100 = 35/65 × 100

workedExamples.title: Identifying scale
workedExamples.prompt: A study of voting patterns in one county is at what scale?
steps: Scale of analysis is the area a study covers: global, regional, national, state or local
Voting patterns within one county cover a small, bounded area
So the scale of analysis is local, even though results may be compared to national patterns

workedExamples.title: Explaining cultural diffusion
workedExamples.prompt: How did hip-hop spread around the world?
steps: It began in the Bronx in the 1970s.
Media and the internet spread it, an example of hierarchical and contagious diffusion.
Local artists adapted it with their own languages and styles.
workedExamples.answer: Hip-hop diffused through media and was reshaped locally.

workedExamples.title: Using the concentric zone model
workedExamples.prompt: Describe Burgess's concentric zone model of a city.
steps: The central business district is at the core.
Surrounding it are rings: transition, working-class housing, middle-class homes and commuters.
The city grows outward from the center.
workedExamples.answer: The city is organized in rings around a central business district.

workedExamples.title: Applying Weber's least-cost theory
workedExamples.prompt: Why do steel mills tend to locate near coal and iron ore?
steps: Raw materials such as iron ore lose weight when processed.
Moving heavy raw materials is expensive.
Locating near them minimizes transportation costs.
workedExamples.answer: Locating near raw materials reduces the cost of transport.

workedExamples.title: Centripetal and centrifugal forces
workedExamples.prompt: Identify one centripetal and one centrifugal force in Belgium.
steps: Centripetal forces unify a state, such as shared national institutions and the capital Brussels.
Centrifugal forces divide a state, such as the language divide between Flemish and French speakers.
Federalism is one way Belgium manages these tensions.
workedExamples.answer: Brussels and federalism unify, while language differences divide.

workedExamples.title: Using Von Thunen's model
workedExamples.prompt: Where would dairy farming be located relative to a city?
steps: Milk is perishable and costly to transport.
Von Thunen predicts intensive, perishable products close to the market.
Land near the city is expensive, so only high-value uses locate there.

hardQuiz.q: A map that uses shading to show data by region, such as population density, is a:

o: The exact position given by coordinates
The position described by its relationship to other places
The reputation and image people hold of a place
The number of people who live in a place
hardQuiz.e: Latitude and longitude give absolute location.

hardQuiz.q: Which is a push factor for migration?
hardQuiz.e: Push factors drive people away from a place.

o: Evenly outward in all directions from a source, like a wave
Only by the migration of people from place to place
Only through trade between neighboring places and regions
From people or places of power or influence to others
hardQuiz.e: Trends often spread from cities to smaller places.

o: Extensive agriculture occurs closest to the market
Intensive agriculture occurs closer to the market
hardQuiz.e: Land near the market is more expensive.

hardQuiz.q: The Burgess concentric zone model describes a city as:
o: Wedges extending out along major transportation routes
Several separate nuclei, each with its own function
Rings around a central business district
A single line of development along one main road

hardQuiz.q: Weber's least-cost theory says firms locate where:
o: Transportation and labor costs are lowest
Land is most expensive and the market is farthest away
Skilled workers are scarce and wages are highest
Competition is greatest and rivals cluster nearby
hardQuiz.e: Firms balance transport, labor and agglomeration.

hardQuiz.q: In core-periphery models, peripheral countries often:
o: Control global finance and set the terms of world trade
Produce only high-tech goods for sale to other countries
Export raw materials and depend on core economies
Have little or no trade with any other countries
hardQuiz.e: The core controls most capital and technology.

hardQuiz.q: State sovereignty means that a state:
o: Has supreme authority over its territory
Has no borders and its territory is open to all
Shares authority over its land with all of its neighbors
Has one ethnic group within its borders
hardQuiz.e: Sovereignty is the basis of the modern state system.

hardQuiz.q: Membership in a supranational organization such as the European Union requires member states to:
o: End all trade with countries outside the organization
Eliminate their own national governments entirely
Share one common culture and national language
Give up some sovereignty in certain areas
hardQuiz.e: States agree to common rules in exchange for benefits.
